title: eng-ml
text:
eng-ml

maya: Heads-up — new model bring-up for gptx-small-zh-int8 showing weird token merges on Simplified Hanzi. Quick zh->en BLEU run dropped ~1.7%. Anyone seen mergey tokens like this?

aj: saw something similar in another quant bring-up last quarter, could be BPE merge table change + quant noise. Can you paste a failing example?

maya: yes — from eval set:

maya: ```
source: 我们已经把设备放在桌子上。
gold: We put the device on the table.
model: We have put the deviceonthe table.
```

maya: notice `deviceonthe` — tokens glued together. tokenizer output below.

maya: ```
Tokenized: ["我", "们", "已", "经", "把", "设", "备放", "在", "桌", "子", "上", "。"]
```

satoshi: whoa `设备放` looks wrong — should be `设`, `备`, `放`. That suggests our merge rules differ from the open-source vocab we onboarded. Which tokenizer file did we load for the int8 variant?

maya: loading `vocab.json` from model package `gptx-small-zh/2024-06-05/int8` in the dedicated bucket.

aj: check whether we accidentally used a Simplified->Traditional normalization step or a custom pretokenizer. Also quant can cause subtle differences in logits distribution but it shouldn't change tokenization. Tokenization is deterministic — so something upstream mutated the vocab.

jun: ran a quick diff between the int8 package and the reference fp16 package. Found modified merges.txt: a stray line `设 备放` inserted at the end (looks like a bad merge entry).

jun: ```
$ git --no-pager diff -- gptx-small-zh/fp16/vocab/merges.txt gptx-small-zh/int8/vocab/merges.txt
+设 备放
```

oliver: that's the smoking gun. How did that get in there? CI should have caught tokenization drift checks.

maya: CI tests for tokenization parity were green because the check compares token count distributions only, not specific token boundaries. Need better tests.

eval-bot: quick-run results: zh->en BLEU baseline (fp16): 31.6, gptx-small-zh-int8: 29.9, delta -1.7. Tokenization mismatch detected in 0.6% of sentences.

aj: plan: 1) roll back int8 package, 2) add strict token-level parity test to onboarding pipeline (exact token sequence match on a 5k seedset), 3) add a preflight that diffs merges.txt against canonical.

maya: agreed. Also re-run quantization with fresh merges.txt and confirm no perf regressions. If that passes, promote.

jun: filing a quick PR to revert the bad artifact and add the diff check: https://git.internal/r/redwood/gptx-small-zh/merge-fix (WIP).

oliver: can we also add a lightweight prompt-level eval to catch combined-word hallucinations like `deviceonthe`? Maybe a simple regex check for long alphabetical fragments in English outputs when source is CJK.

aj: good idea. Add a rule: flag any output with contiguous [A-Za-z]{8,} when source contains CJK characters. Low false positive and catches glue-ups.

maya: i'm re-running the eval now after swapping merges.txt back. will post numbers in ~10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(10 minutes later)

maya: rerun complete. eval-bot summary attached.

maya: ```
eval-bot: zh->en BLEU gptx-small-zh-int8 (fixed merges): 31.4 (delta -0.2 vs fp16), token mismatch 0.01%
```

aj: looks good. can we add a CI gate: if token mismatch > 0.05% fail packaging?

oliver: yep, and add a human review step for any merges.txt changes in model packaging PRs.

jun: PR merged, packaging re-run triggered. build pipeline will now fail on token diffs > 0.05% and on suspicious merge entries (non-BMP or multi-char tokens).

maya: thanks all. follow-ups: ticket for CI tests (#ML-1129), add regex heuristic to eval harness (#ML-1130), and retro to SRE for packaging automation.

aj: adding to next week retro. :white_check_mark:

oliver: :eyes: good catch, maya and jun.

maya: tagging @eng-platform to review packaging steps.

end of thread.
